title: Durability of Parameters Associated With Endurance Running in Marathoners
population: 2024 London Marathon participants (11 male; age 41 +/- 12 y; finish 3:17 +/- 0:32 h:min)
findings: Within-subject comparison of fresh (PRE) vs after a 90-min run at lactate-threshold speed (POST).
VO2peak fell from 56.7 +/- 7.2 to 53.4 +/- 6.3 mL/kg/min and sLT fell from 12.8 +/- 2.0 to 12.1 +/- 2.2 km/h (both p<0.001), a decline of about 5.5% in mean sLT.
Running economy and fractional utilisation at LT did not change (p>0.05).
Percentage change in sLT correlated with marathon performance (r=0.680, p<0.01): smaller deterioration went with faster marathon times.
limitations: 18 mostly recreational marathoners; single laboratory fatiguing protocol with no between-condition randomisation; correlation only; RE not changing differs from other studies using other protocols.
implications: Estimate a runner's durability as the percent decline of threshold speed after about 90 min at threshold pace (about 5.5% on average here: 12.8 to 12.1 km/h) and feed it into marathon prediction.
Where no lab test exists, use the late-run decoupling ratio as a proxy and flag the proxy as lower confidence (the link between the two has not been shown in this paper).

verification.notes: Crossref (online 2025-10-23, print 2025 Nov) and PubMed match. Design changed from experimental-crossover to other: single-group PRE/POST with correlation. 'About 5%' made explicit as 5.5% from the reported means.
